newsitem.title: UK: UK Building Societes Bill seen re-published in Dec.
newsitem.headline: UK Building Societes Bill seen re-published in Dec.

text.p: The UK Treasury said it is aiming to re-publish in early December the amended Building Societies Bill which was unexpectedly omitted from the government programme in the new parliamentary session.

The revised bill would take into account representations made to the Treasury over the summer, and could be included in the current parliamentary session depending on time available and how much support it received.
The government came under fire at a conference on Tuesday from the opposition Labour Party's city spokesman, Mike O'Brien, for what he described as the bill's "extraordinary" omission.

Angela Knight, economic secretary to the Treasury, said that issues such as fraud and Dunblane, a Scottish city where the murder of a 16 young schoolchildren prompted demands for a ban on handguns and combat knives, were higher up the political agenda than the Building Societies Bill.

The new bill is essentially a deregulatory measure which will give societies more freedom as long as 75 percent of their lending is on housing and they raise a minimum of 50 percent of their funds from their members.
